---
title: "Run MISP 3.0 in Ubuntu on macOS with Apple container"
---

Use Apple's `container` tool to run a persistent Ubuntu 24.04 LTS container machine on your Mac.
Ubuntu runs the services that MISP needs, including Apache, MariaDB, Redis, and Supervisor.
This walkthrough uses the [MISP `3.0_wip` Ubuntu installer](../install-ubuntu/index.qmd#ubuntu-install-run) for a local evaluation instance.

::: {.callout-note}
You need an Apple silicon Mac with macOS 26 or later and Apple `container` 1.7.1 or later.
Install Apple's signed package and check which version is installed.
The commands follow Apple's 1.7.1 reference, and the Ubuntu image recipe was checked on Linux x86_64.
Verify machine boot, the installer, DNS, and browser access on your Mac. [Apple container requirements](https://github.com/apple/container/blob/1.7.1/README.md#get-started) · [Apple releases](https://github.com/apple/container/releases)
:::

## Set up the Mac {#apple-container-host}

Run the host commands in a dedicated Terminal tab.
Container machines can mount your macOS home directory and forward your SSH agent.
This example disables the home mount and clears the SSH agent environment variable for this tab.
Use a trusted base image and review the installer before running it with `sudo`. [Apple container machine documentation](https://github.com/apple/container/blob/1.7.1/docs/container-machine.md)

```bash
unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK
container --version
container system start
```

Use Apple's embedded DNS to give the instance the stable name `misp-ubuntu.test`.
In `~/.config/container/config.toml` on the Mac, add or update the `[dns]` section.
If you already configured a local domain and its macOS resolver, skip this setup and substitute that domain throughout the guide.

```toml
[dns]
domain = "test"
```

Restart Apple's container service when you can interrupt any other running containers.
Register the matching resolver on macOS. [Apple container DNS setup](https://github.com/apple/container/blob/1.7.1/docs/networking.md#set-up-dns-based-container-names)

```bash
container system stop
container system start
sudo container system dns create test
```

## Build and boot an Ubuntu container machine {#apple-container-machine}

On the Mac, create a dedicated build directory and save the following as `Dockerfile`.
The official Ubuntu image supplies the Linux filesystem.
Adding `systemd-sysv` gives the machine the `/sbin/init` entry point required to run Linux services.
The setup follows Apple's [Ubuntu container machine example](https://github.com/apple/container/blob/1.7.1/docs/container-machine.md#bring-your-own-image).

```dockerfile
FROM ubuntu:24.04

ENV container=container

RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
      ca-certificates curl dbus iproute2 less openssl procps sudo systemd systemd-sysv && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

RUN truncate -s 0 /etc/machine-id /var/lib/dbus/machine-id && \
    systemctl set-default multi-user.target && \
    systemctl mask dev-hugepages.mount sys-fs-fuse-connections.mount \
      systemd-update-utmp.service systemd-tmpfiles-setup.service console-getty.service

STOPSIGNAL SIGRTMIN+3
```

From the build directory on your Mac, build and boot the machine.
The example allocates four virtual CPUs and 8 GiB of memory. [MISP sizing guidance](../requirements/index.qmd#sizing-your-misp-instance)

```bash
container build -t local/misp-ubuntu-machine:24.04 .
container machine create --name misp-ubuntu --cpus 4 --memory 8G \
  --home-mount none local/misp-ubuntu-machine:24.04
container machine list
container machine run -n misp-ubuntu
```

In the **Ubuntu shell**, check the release, architecture, and init process.
Continue once Ubuntu reports 24.04, the architecture is `aarch64`, and PID 1 is `systemd`.
Check that the guest has `sudo` and no forwarded SSH agent.

```bash
cat /etc/os-release
uname -m
ps -p 1 -o comm=
sudo -n true
test -z "${SSH_AUTH_SOCK:-}"
```

If boot or guest setup fails, check `container machine logs --boot misp-ubuntu` from the Mac. [Apple container machine commands](https://github.com/apple/container/blob/1.7.1/docs/command-reference.md#container-machine-management)

## Install MISP inside Ubuntu {#apple-container-install}

From the **Ubuntu shell**, generate a certificate for the lab hostname and keep the private key inside Ubuntu.
Use a certificate from your organization's CA instead if clients already trust that CA.

```bash
sudo openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:2048 -noenc -days 90 \
  -subj '/CN=misp-ubuntu.test' \
  -addext 'subjectAltName=DNS:misp-ubuntu.test' \
  -keyout /etc/ssl/private/misp-ubuntu.key \
  -out /etc/ssl/certs/misp-ubuntu.crt
sudo chmod 0600 /etc/ssl/private/misp-ubuntu.key
sudo chmod 0644 /etc/ssl/certs/misp-ubuntu.crt
```

Download and review the `3.0_wip` installer inside Ubuntu.
Use the same hostname in the certificate, the Apache virtual host, and MISP's base URL. [Ubuntu installer options](../install-ubuntu/index.qmd#ubuntu-install-run)

```bash
cd "$HOME"
curl --fail --location --output INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MISP/MISP/3.0_wip/INSTALL/INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh
less INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh
sudo env \
  MISP_DOMAIN=misp-ubuntu.test \
  MISP_BASEURL=https://misp-ubuntu.test \
  PATH_TO_SSL_CERT=/etc/ssl/certs/misp-ubuntu.crt \
  PATH_TO_SSL_KEY=/etc/ssl/private/misp-ubuntu.key \
  GPG_EMAIL_ADDRESS=misp@misp-ubuntu.test \
  bash ./INSTALL.ubuntu2404.sh
```

Check Apache, MariaDB, Redis, the workers, and the application schema inside Ubuntu.

```bash
sudo apache2ctl configtest
sudo systemctl is-active apache2 mariadb redis-server supervisor
sudo supervisorctl status 'misp-workers:*'
sudo -u www-data /var/www/MISP/app/Console/cake Admin schemaDiagnostics
sudo -u www-data git -C /var/www/MISP rev-parse HEAD
```

Check for zero pending and failed migrations and confirm the six workers are running.
Read the initial account credentials from the root-only `/root/misp_settings.txt` inside Ubuntu.
The installation log can also contain credentials. [Ubuntu installation checks](../install-ubuntu/index.qmd#ubuntu-install-check)

## Open MISP from the Mac {#apple-container-access}

In the **Mac Terminal**, copy the public certificate out of Ubuntu and use it to verify the first HTTPS request.
The machine has its own IP address on Apple's default network. Use `misp-ubuntu.test` in the browser and API clients.

```bash
container machine run -n misp-ubuntu -- cat /etc/ssl/certs/misp-ubuntu.crt > misp-ubuntu.crt
dscacheutil -q host -a name misp-ubuntu.test
curl --cacert ./misp-ubuntu.crt --fail --silent --show-error \
  --output /dev/null https://misp-ubuntu.test/users/login
```

If name resolution fails, compare the IP shown by `container machine list` with the macOS lookup and check both parts of the [Apple DNS setup](https://github.com/apple/container/blob/1.7.1/docs/networking.md#set-up-dns-based-container-names).
For browser access with the lab certificate, import its public certificate into your login keychain and set SSL trust for that certificate.
Open **https://misp-ubuntu.test**, sign in, change the bootstrap password, and create an unpublished, organization-only test event. [Certificate trust in Keychain Access](https://support.apple.com/guide/keychain-access/change-the-trust-settings-of-a-certificate-kyca11871/mac) · [First steps after login](../quick-start/index.qmd#first-steps-after-login)

## Stop, resume, and back up the machine {#apple-container-lifecycle}

Exit the Ubuntu shell when you are done with that session.
From the Mac, stop the machine when you want to free its resources.
Opening the machine again starts Ubuntu and its enabled services.

```bash
container machine stop misp-ubuntu
container machine run -n misp-ubuntu
```

The machine preserves its Linux filesystem, including the MISP database and configuration, across stop and start.
Store [MISP backups](../administration/index.qmd#admin-backup-recovery) outside the machine before deleting it.
`container machine delete misp-ubuntu` removes its persistent filesystem.
Remove the lab certificate from your Mac's keychain when you retire the instance.
